questions.prompt: The word “history” comes from a Greek word. Which one, and what does it mean?
questions.explanation: The textbook states that the term history is derived from the Greek word “Istoria”, which means ‘learning by enquiry’.

questions.prompt: Which discipline studies human ancestors and their evolution through fossil remains?
questions.explanation: Palaeoanthropology is defined as the study of human ancestors and their evolution by the study of fossil remains. Archaeology, by contrast, studies the human past through material remains.

questions.prompt: Which salt did the Egyptians use to preserve dead bodies?
questions.explanation: The Egyptians preserved dead bodies using Natron salt, a combination of sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate.

questions.prompt: Arikkamedu, a Sangam Age port, is located near which city?
questions.explanation: Arikkamedu, near Puducherry, is a Sangam Age port excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.prompt: What were the earliest coins used in India, and what were they mostly made of?
questions.explanation: Punch-marked coins are the earliest coins used in India. They are mostly made of silver and carry numerous punched symbols, which is how they got the name.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Society of Friends, whose members are known as Quakers?
questions.explanation: George Fox founded the Society of Friends in England. Quakers emphasised the Holy Spirit and rejected outward rites and an ordained ministry.

questions.prompt: Which city had more than 50 mills in 1802?
questions.explanation: Among the major factory centres, the most notable was Manchester, which had more than 50 mills in 1802.

questions.prompt: Under the Ryotwari system, at what share of the produce did the government fix its demand?
questions.explanation: Under the Ryotwari system the settlement was made directly with the ryots and the government fixed the demand at 45% to 55% of the produce.

questions.prompt: Whose idea was the Mahalwari system?
questions.explanation: The Mahalwari system was described as the brainchild of Holt Mackenzie. Bentinck later suggested changes to it, guided by Robert Martins Bird.

questions.prompt: At which railway station was Gandhi thrown out of a first class compartment?
questions.explanation: On his journey from Durban to Pretoria, Gandhi was physically thrown out of the first class compartment at Pietermaritzburg Railway Station.

questions.prompt: Whom did Gandhi regard as his political guru?
questions.explanation: Gandhi regarded Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political guru, and on Gokhale’s advice travelled across India before entering politics.

questions.prompt: In which city was the Khilafat Committee formed?
questions.explanation: A Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 to defend the Khalifa’s temporal powers.

questions.prompt: According to Our Pasts – I, where was rice first grown?
options: To the north of the Vindhyas
On the banks of the Indus
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the places where rice was first grown are to the north of the Vindhyas.

questions.prompt: What age range was required of members of the sabha?
options: Over 40 years, with no upper limit
questions.explanation: The inscription lists the qualifications for sabha membership, including that members should be between 35 and 70 years of age.

questions.prompt: How were paintings fitted into a Mughal manuscript?
options: The scribe left blank spaces on nearby pages and separately executed paintings were inserted
Painters worked directly on the finished text pages
Paintings were bound in a separate volume from the text
Paintings were printed onto the page after the text was written
questions.explanation: When scenes were to be given visual expression, the scribe left blank spaces on nearby pages, and paintings executed separately by artists were inserted to accompany the words.

questions.prompt: When did Gandhi leave for South Africa?

questions.prompt: When was the Khilafat Committee formed in Bombay?
questions.explanation: A Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919, after the First World War ended with the defeat of Ottoman Turkey.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Mahalwari system introduced?
questions.explanation: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 in the Ganga Valley, the North-West Province, parts of Central India and Punjab. Bentinck suggested changes to it in 1833.

questions.prompt: In which year did Italy invade Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935 and Albania in 1939. Emperor Haile Selassie appealed to the League of Nations but got no help.

questions.prompt: In which year did Hitler invade Austria and Czechoslovakia?
questions.explanation: In 1938 Hitler invaded Austria and Czechoslovakia, claiming that German-speaking people — such as those in the Sudetenland — should be united into one nation.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act passed?
questions.explanation: Three laws are listed as protecting archaeological remains in India: the Indian Treasure Trove Act (1878), the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act (1958) and the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act (1972).

questions.prompt: Native Americans resisted attempts to make them work on the plantations. What did European planters in the southern colonies do as a result?
options: They acquired enslaved people from Africa
They recruited indentured labour from Britain
They moved their plantations to the northern colonies
questions.explanation: Because Native Americans resisted plantation labour, planters — chiefly of tobacco, in Virginia, the Carolinas and Georgia — resorted to acquiring slaves from Africa in their search for labour.

questions.prompt: The Company received ₹ 22.5 million from Mir Jafar between 1757 and 1760. What does the textbook say this money went on to do?
options: It was invested to propel the industrial revolution in Britain and mechanise its textile industry
It was used to build railways across Bengal
It was returned to the Nawab’s treasury after Buxar
It funded the Company’s trade in China
questions.explanation: The same money was later invested to propel the industrial revolution in Britain, which rapidly mechanised the British textile industry — while India was led towards de-industrialisation.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Versailles imposed penal reparations on Germany. What consequence does the textbook draw from the post-war crisis?
options: The rise of extreme right-wing dictatorships in Italy, Germany and Spain
The immediate collapse of the League of Nations
The unification of Austria and Germany in 1919
The end of colonial rule in Asia and Africa
questions.explanation: Penal reparations caused great discontent in Germany, and the problems many countries faced in the post-war decades led to the rise of extreme right-wing dictatorships in Italy (Mussolini), Germany (Hitler) and Spain (Franco).

questions.prompt: Violence spread during the Rowlatt satyagraha. What did Mahatma Gandhi do?
options: He extended the movement to the villages
He asked satyagrahis to defend themselves
questions.explanation: Seeing violence spread — and the government responding with floggings and the bombing of villages around Gujranwala — Mahatma Gandhi called off the movement.

questions.prompt: In most areas the Ryotwari land revenue was fixed excessively high. What was the effect on the cultivators?
options: They were hardly left with bare maintenance even in the best of seasons
They were able to save and buy more land
They shifted to cultivating cash crops for export
They were protected because the Zamindars paid the difference
questions.explanation: The textbook states that in most areas the land revenue fixed was excessive, and the ryots were hardly left with bare maintenance even in the best of seasons — under this system the government exploited the farmers instead of the Zamindars.

questions.prompt: Production rose sharply in industrial Britain. What followed, according to the textbook?
options: New networks of canals, roads and railroads were built
Factories moved away from the major towns
Coal production fell as machines replaced it
The division of labour was abandoned
questions.explanation: As production increased, raw materials had to be brought from afar and goods carried to markets, so new networks of canals, roads and railroads were built — helped by macadamised roads and George Stephenson’s steam locomotive.
